summary: Goat Island Light at Cape Porpoise: first lit in the 1830s, the brick tower of 1859, staffed until 1991, now owned by a conservation trust.

access.note: Reached by boat. Grounds open in summer; dwelling and tower closed; keepers give tower tours when at home.

events.note: First light shown in August 1833 (LighthouseFriends); NRHP gives 1833 as the year established. Other sources give 1834 and 1835.
Present brick tower, 25 ft (7.6 m) to the base of the lantern; keeper's house also dated 1859 (NRHP).
Fifth-order Franklin lamps placed inside the 1859 lens.
Goat Island Light was used to set the range for the cruiser New York's speed trial course, 22 May 1893.
Gale; waves crossed the island and damaged the walkway and boat slip.
Fog bell replaced by a horn sounding every twenty seconds.
Blizzard of 1978 swept away the walkway between the keeper's quarters and the tower.
National Register of Historic Places, March 1988 (KCT); NRHP nomination prepared 1987.
Last keeper left in the fall of 1991 (LighthouseFriends; roster ends 1991). USLHS record gives automation in 1990.
Title passed from the United States to the Kennebunkport Conservation Trust under the Maine Lights Program (leased from 1992).
Solar array with battery bank installed to power the light and horn.
Trust restoration: walkway rebuilt, bell tower reconstructed, keeper's quarters refurbished; $1 million project.
Submarine power cable from the mainland failed (November 2022).
Solar panels installed to power the island; generators had supplied some power.

corrections.why: The standing brick tower was built in 1859 (NRHP; USLHS 'Year Tower Established: 1859'). The record's 1835 belongs to the first, rubblestone tower.
USLHS gives 'Year Automated: 1990', but its own roster has Bradley Culp keeping the light until 1991, and LighthouseFriends says it stayed staffed until the fall of 1991. Flagged for human review.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's spread of first-year dates (1834, 1835, 1859) mixes the first tower with the present brick tower of 1859. NRHP and LighthouseFriends give 1833 for the first light; the Trust gives 1834 for the appropriation and 1835 for completion; USLHS gives 1835 for establishment. The sources do not settle the first year, and the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the first year: NRHP and LighthouseFriends 1833, the record's Rowlett 1834, the Trust 1834 for the appropriation and 1835 for completion, USLHS 1835 (established). The appropriation is 1831 (LighthouseFriends) or 1834 (Trust). Keeper's quarters: 1859 (NRHP) against 1860 (USLHS 'Year Keeper's Quarters: 1860' and the Trust's 1860 remodel). Acreage: 7.6 (Trust), 7.7 nominated (NRHP), about three and a half (LighthouseFriends). Automation: 1990 (USLHS) against fall 1991 (LighthouseFriends and the roster). The 1893 speed-trial positions are OCR text; the start-point distance is unreadable ('4£ miles') and is left out. The wreck totals (46 wrecks, 28 losses, 229 aboard) come from LighthouseFriends without a stated source. The 1921 death on the island (LighthouseFriends) found no matching newspaper hit in a 1921 search. Not used: the 1894 Lighthouse Board item '2,000 tons of stone quarried on Goat Island' (it is Oakland Harbor, California); the Portland Press 1903 launch that passed 'Goat island light' near Portsmouth (a different Goat Island). Caretakers living on the island are not named (Trust names them in its public role only; LighthouseFriends names two earlier caretakers, not used). LighthouseFriends' ghost stories are left out. Fiscal-year attribution of the FY1899 repair list rests on the report's '1899' page header; the surrounding estimates look ahead to 1900. OCR of the 1893 'Goat Island' passage (scan) is checked against the cached page, not the page image. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the speed-trial run was on 22 May 1893 (the 23 May Press reports it; the text now says so). LighthouseFriends prints Lavaughn Bryant as "at least 1958 - 1962" where the USLHS gives "at least 1957-1962"; the roster keeps the USLHS span. LighthouseFriends prose is now paraphrased; the inspection wording it quotes from public reports is kept and attributed to LighthouseFriends as quoting them.
